correctness.rationale: For a set-sized M⊨ZFC and set I with at least two coordinates, coordinatewise direct-power membership fibres are Cartesian boxes ∏ A_i. Restrict a separator parent to two coordinates with two possible finite-cardinality values each; Separation requires the selected corners to form a rectangle. Let F(n) be the eventual-constant Boolean cardinality test θ, and R(a,b)↔F(ab). A nonempty symmetric rectangular relation is A×A; because F(n)=F(n⋅1), this entails F(1)=1 and F(ab)=F(a)F(b). The zero relation gives ⊥; if F(0)=1 multiplicativity gives ⊤. For F(0)=0, eventual constancy forces either F positive-integers=1 (E1) or F indicator of {1} (E1∧¬E2): an excluded positive n has arbitrarily large multiples, and an included n≥2 has arbitrarily large powers. Those four predicates separate coordinatewise using internal ZFC Separation and external choice, including infinite I. Every other F has a nonrectangular 2×2 matrix with two opposite accepted and a rejected cross-corner, realized by a parent with exactly four members. Any membership box of at most three members can vary in only one coordinate and every subset remains a box, giving sharp minimality for any formula.
